question.text: How many cumulative confirmed measles cases will Mexico's daily measles bulletin report on November 26, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the cumulative number of confirmed measles cases for 2025–2026 ("Total casos confirmados acumulados 2025-2026") stated in Mexico's Secretaría de Salud daily measles bulletin ("Informe Diario de Sarampión"), as listed at https://www.gob.mx/salud/documentos/informe-diario-del-brote-de-sarampion-en-mexico-2026. The edition used is the most recent one dated on or before 26 November 2026, where an edition's date is the date given in its own line "Información preliminar con fecha [date] de 2026, con corte a las 11:00 horas" (e.g. the edition dated 11 November 2026 stated 20,552 confirmed cases). If that PDF cannot be accessed, the figure reported for that same edition by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) is used.
question.fine_print: The value used is the combined 2025–2026 cumulative confirmed total (the 2025 and 2026 subtotals added together), not the 2026-only subtotal. Corrections or revisions appearing in bulletins dated after 26 November 2026 do not affect resolution.

research:
I couldn't read the official PDFs directly (they are image-based), so the figures below come from news reports that cite them. The latest figure is **20,701 confirmed cases**, from the bulletin dated 12 November 2026. That is 149 more than the 20,552 given as the 11 November figure, and already 151 above the bottom of the question's range.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The gob.mx index's newest entry is "Informe diario, corte al 12 de noviembre de 2026" ([Informe_diario_12_11_2026.pdf](https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/1116356/Informe_diario_12_11_2026.pdf)). There is no 13 November edition yet. Earlier editions listed: 15-16, 19-23 and 26-30 October, and 3-6 and 9-11 November. [index](https://www.gob.mx/salud/documentos/informe-diario-del-brote-de-sarampion-en-mexico-2026)
- The PDFs could not be read as text. The 12 November figures, as reported by others:
  - 46,598 notified EFE (febrile rash illness) cases
  - **20,701 confirmed** cases
  - 50 deaths

  [Proceso](https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/2026/11/13/mexico-se-aproxima-al-cierre-del-brote-de-sarampion-anuncia-kershenobich-383705.html); [El Economista via news API](https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/politica/sarampion-mexico-brote-suma-50-muertes-caida-cobertura-vacunacion-20261115-844087.html); [Yahoo](https://es-us.noticias.yahoo.com/sarampi%C3%B3n-m%C3%A9xico-brote-suma-50-131235235.html)
- Date mismatch: Milenio gives the 20,552 figure (46,564 EFE, 25,119 discarded, **893 under study**) as the 10 November cut-off, while the question says 11 November. [Milenio](https://www.milenio.com/estados/mexico-supera-20-mil-casos-sarampion-noviembre-2026)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The figure is already 20,701. About 9 weekday bulletins are still possible from 13 to 26 November (13, 17-20 and 23-26 November). Monday 16 November is likely a federal holiday (Revolution Day, observed on the third Monday), so there is probably no bulletin today. I have not confirmed this.
- The total cannot realistically go down. The main uncertainty is how big the batch confirmations from the backlog will be.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15: Several outlets repeat 20,701 cases and 50 deaths as of 12 November. Jalisco has 8,272 cases, up from 8,130 in the earlier bulletin, so most of the jump came from Jalisco. [Cadena Política](https://cadenapolitica.com/2026/11/15/el-brote-de-sarampion-en-mexico-deja-50-muertes-y-mas-de-20000-casos-confirmados/); [El Chamuco](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/11/15/mexico-registra-seis-casos-activos-de-sarampion-salud-reporta-90-de-cobertura-de-vacunacion/)
- 2026-11-13: Health Secretary Kershenobich said the outbreak is nearing its end:
  - Only **6 active cases** (5 in Chiapas, 1 in Quintana Roo).
  - 12 of 32 states have gone at least 12 weeks without active cases.
  - Formal closure is targeted for the second half of 2027.

  [Proceso](https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/2026/11/13/mexico-se-aproxima-al-cierre-del-brote-de-sarampion-anuncia-kershenobich-383705.html)
- 2026-11-10/11: That bulletin added **115 cases from earlier weeks** (Jalisco 81, Chiapas 34) and none confirmed that day. Officials said such jumps "do not necessarily represent recent infections." The final-classification strategy has been running since 4 September. [Milenio](https://www.milenio.com/estados/mexico-supera-20-mil-casos-sarampion-noviembre-2026)
- 2026-11-10 to 13: PAHO's commission reviewed the US and Mexico. The US was reported to have lost elimination status, and a decision on Mexico is expected the week of 16 November. [Deccan Chronicle](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/world/us-and-mexico-risk-losing-major-health-victory-what-you-need-to-know-2004449); [IBTimes](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/us-loses-measles-elimination-status-year-long-transmission-1832280)

## 4. Base rates and trajectory
Cumulative 2025-2026 confirmed cases:

| Date | Total | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 11 Sep | 19,536 | [Excélsior](https://www.excelsior.com.mx/nacional/sarampion-mexico-septiembre-2026) |
| 19 Oct | 20,332 | question background |
| 26 Oct | 20,375 | question background |
| 5 Nov | 20,410 | question background |
| ~8 Nov cut-off | 20,410 (2026: 13,796) | [Global Risk Atlas](https://globalriskatlas.com/mexico-20-410-casos-confirmados-de-sarampion-y-50-muertes-desde-2025/) |
| 10/11 Nov | 20,552 | [Milenio](https://www.milenio.com/estados/mexico-supera-20-mil-casos-sarampion-noviembre-2026) |
| 12 Nov | 20,701 | [Proceso](https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/2026/11/13/mexico-se-aproxima-al-cierre-del-brote-de-sarampion-anuncia-kershenobich-383705.html) |

What the series shows:
- Over 14-day windows, growth ranged from about +43 (19 Oct to 2 Nov) to about +291 (29 Oct to 12 Nov).
- From 11 September to 12 November the total rose about 1,165, or roughly 19 a day, with long flat stretches broken by batches of 23, 115 and 149.
- Growth sped up during the PAHO review week, mostly from the backlog rather than new spread. About 890-910 cases were still under study around 10-11 November.
- Seasonality: the 2025-2026 series is the only comparable record. Earlier years had almost no measles in Mexico, so there is no useful seasonal baseline. New transmission is clearly fading, with only 6 active cases.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or expert forecast on Mexico's cumulative total. The Kalshi measles markets supplied are about US case counts and US elimination status (Yes at 0.98), so they do not match this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Week of 2026-11-16: PAHO is expected to announce its decision on Mexico's elimination status. That could change how fast the ministry keeps clearing the backlog. [Deccan Chronicle](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/world/us-and-mexico-risk-losing-major-health-victory-what-you-need-to-know-2004449)
- The final-classification batches (mostly Jalisco and Chiapas) are the main thing driving the number. With about 900 cases under study, one or two more batches of 100 or more within the window are plausible.
- Bulletins can be delayed: none has been posted for 13 November so far. If 26 November is not published, resolution falls back to the latest edition dated before it.
- Weather is not relevant.

## 2. Current status

- Up to 9 more weekday editions could come out between 13 and 26 Nov. 16 Nov is Mexico's Revolution Day holiday, and I'd guess there may be no bulletin that day, but I haven't confirmed that.
- Under-study cases stood at about 900 on 11 Nov. That is the pool any further batch confirmations would come from.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15: Press reports repeat 20,701 cases and 50 deaths. 12 of 32 states have gone at least 12 weeks without active cases, and vaccination coverage is 90%. I found no announced outcome for Mexico. [Deccan Chronicle](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/world/us-and-mexico-risk-losing-major-health-victory-what-you-need-to-know-2004449), [IBTimes](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/us-loses-measles-elimination-status-year-long-transmission-1832280)
- 2026-11-05: 20,410 cases. [Global Risk Atlas](https://globalriskatlas.com/mexico-20-410-casos-confirmados-de-sarampion-y-50-muertes-desde-2025/)
- 2026-10-22: 20,332 cases (13,718 in 2026). [Por Esto](https://www.poresto.com/campeche/2026/10/22/alerta-sarampion-campeche-confirman-casos-ano.html)

## 4. Base rates and trajectory
- Cumulative confirmed total: 20,332 (19 to 22 Oct), 20,375 (26 Oct), 20,410 (5 Nov), 20,552 (11 Nov), 20,701 (12 Nov).
- Increases over periods of about 10 days:
  - 26 Oct to 5 Nov: +35 (about 3.5 per day)
  - 1 to 11 Nov: about +140
  - 2 to 12 Nov: about +290
- The pace has picked up sharply in the last two editions: +142 and then +149, driven by batch "final classification" of older cases.
- New reporting is small: notified EFE rose only 16 (46,582 to 46,598) between 11 and 12 Nov. Almost all growth is backlog being reclassified, not new transmission.
- Simple scenarios (my arithmetic, not a forecast):
  - Back to the late-October pace (about 5 per edition, 9 editions): about 20,750.
  - About 150 per edition continuing: well above the range ceiling of 21,350. Even 70 per edition for 9 editions would add about 630, giving about 21,330.
  - The hard limit: the under-study pool is about 900, so roughly 21,600 is the maximum. Historically about 44% of notified cases were confirmed.
- Seasonality: no useful history, because this outbreak started in February 2025. Transmission is fading (single-digit to low-twenties weekly EFE notifications), so the movement depends on administrative reclassification rather than on the season.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or expert forecast on Mexico's cumulative count.
- The Kalshi markets provided all concern US measles counts or US elimination status (98% Yes on the US losing status), so they don't match this question.
- PAHO situation report #15 (data through epidemiological week 43): 13,761 confirmed 2026 cases and 23 deaths in Mexico (from the question background, not verified independently).

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- PAHO's decision on Mexico's elimination status is expected this week. It could speed up or slow down the clearing of the classification backlog.
- Daily bulletins for 13 Nov to 26 Nov (weekdays). Watch for notes about batches "de semanas anteriores" and for how fast the under-study count falls.
- 16 Nov holiday: there may be no bulletin that day, and publication may lag (the 13 Nov edition was still not posted on 16 Nov).
- Weather is not relevant.

(a) About 10 days remain until the edition dated 26 November 2026 is published. Resolution is around 27 November. The window covers roughly 9 weekday bulletins (13, 17-20 and 23-26 November), with 16 November likely a holiday.

(b) The latest known value is 20,701 confirmed cases (2025-2026 combined), from the bulletin dated 12 November 2026, as reported by Proceso and El Economista.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be 20,701.

(d) Trends point in different directions:
- Over the last week (5 to 12 November) the total rose by 291, almost all of it batch reclassification from Jalisco and Chiapas during the PAHO review week. Repeating that pace over two weeks would give about 21,280.
- The slower 19 October to 5 November pace (about 4.6 a day) gives about 20,770.
- The 11 September to 12 November average (about 19 a day) gives about 20,970.
- Under-study cases fell to roughly 750-850. With about 44% eventually confirmed, the remaining backlog implies roughly 300-400 more confirmations at most, spread over an unknown period.

(e) Over 14-day windows since September, the total has moved between about +43 and +291. Movement comes in lumps: long flat stretches, then batches of 23, 115 and 149.

(f) There are no markets or expert forecasts on this quantity. Officials say only 6 cases are active, so new transmission adds little. The backlog-clearing strategy is the main driver, and it may slow now that the PAHO review has ended, or continue toward final classification.

(g) Scenarios:
- Low: the ministry pauses final classification after PAHO's decision and only a handful of new cases are confirmed, leaving the total near 20,705-20,720. A late 26 November bulletin would also make an earlier edition decisive.
- High: a large Jalisco and Chiapas batch clears most of the remaining backlog before year-end reporting, adding 400 or more and pushing the total above 21,100.
